state.meaning: A move that fixed what it aimed at and broke something else is not an improvement.

defects: Both seeds have a tall, narrow ovoid-to-columnar crown with a rounded-pointed top. The crown is clearly taller than wide (about 0.6 width:height) and fills about 70-75% of the tree's height. The reference has a broad, dome-to-flat-topped crown that is about as wide as it is tall or wider, and fills about 55-60% of the height.

In neither seed does the bole split into two co-dominant leaders in a narrow V. A pale central stem keeps rising into the crown, with lateral limbs branching off it. The reference has a clear two-leader V-fork at about 40-45% of the height.
The visible limbs stay steeply ascending all the way to the crown edge. None fan outward and arch to near-horizontal or droop, as the reference limbs do, most clearly on the reference's right side.
The crown edge is a uniform fuzzy fringe of foliage with upward-pointing branch tips. It lacks the flat-to-drooping, layered, lacy sprays with separate tips against the sky seen in the reference.

The foliage reads as a dense, mostly solid mass, with little sky and only scattered limb segments showing through. The reference crown is open, with sky and the dark limb structure visible across much of it.
observations: The trunk is pale lavender-grey, even in tone and smooth-outlined, with no furrows or plates, in both seeds. This matches the reference's pale, even-toned bole.

Each seed has a single straight, slender bole with no branches below the crown. The clear bole is about 25-30% of the tree's height, compared with about 40% in the reference, and the reference's short stub on the left below the fork is absent.
No narrow two-leader V is visible. A central pale stem continues upward inside the crown (render-0 up to about y=800; render-1 up to about y=830), with side limbs splitting off it.
The crown outline is a tall ovoid or egg shape, clearly taller than wide, with a narrowing top. The reference is broad, domed and flat-topped.
The visible limbs go up at steep angles right to the crown periphery, with no outward arching or drooping at the edge.
The crown edge has fine fuzzy texture, but no layered horizontal or drooping sprays with distinct tips against the sky.
The crown is dense and largely opaque. The reference crown is open and see-through, with the dark scaffold limbs visible.
Individual leaf shape cannot be resolved in either the renders or the reference at this distance.
The trunk base flares slightly in both seeds. There is no darker base tone, but the inventory leaves the darkening's cause undetermined and it may be shadow or moss.
Overall crown character reads as a narrow ovoid broadleaf, not a mature open-grown beech. The crown shape, fork, limb arching and openness all differ from the reference.

No traits are listed in known_gaps, so every core trait was assessed.
render-0 (seed 1) and render-1 (seed 42) share the same overall habit: a pale smooth clear bole beneath a tall ovoid, dense crown. Most judgements therefore apply to both seeds.
reference-0 shows a broad, open, flat-domed beech with a V-fork and dark arching limbs. The background trees and wooden frames were ignored.
anchor-0 was used only as the finish-quality floor. Rendering finish at least matches that floor. The failures are morphological, not about photorealism.

Leaf colour differs slightly: the renders are a mid-to-deep green and the reference is a fresh yellow-green. The inventory classes this as variation (fresh-yellow-green-leaf-colour), so it is not a defect.
The reference's crown asymmetry and lower drooping foliage are variation traits and were not required.

defects: Both seeds render a narrow columnar crown with a pointed top, like a Lombardy poplar. The crown is about 2.5-3x taller than it is wide. The reference shows a broad, domed to flat-topped crown that is about as wide as it is tall.
Foliage starts about 10-15% up the tree in both seeds. The reference has a clear, branch-free bole for about 40% of its height.
The trunk splits low, at about 10-15% of the height, into three or more steep, near-parallel stems. The reference splits into two co-dominant leaders in a narrow V at about 40-45% of the height.
The limbs stay steeply upright up to the crown edge. They never fan outward or arch to near-horizontal and droop, as the reference limbs do.
The crown edge is a uniform fuzzy fringe of upright foliage. It lacks the reference's flat-to-drooping, layered sprays with individual spray tips standing out against the sky.
The foliage is a dense, mostly solid mass. Little sky or internal branch structure shows through, whereas the reference crown is open and translucent.
observations: Crown silhouette: both renders show a tall, narrow column with a pointed top (width about 0.35-0.4 of height). The reference crown is broad and domed, about as wide as it is tall or wider.
The clear bole ends at about 10-15% of the tree's height in both renders, versus about 40% in the reference.
Both renders split low into several steep, parallel stems. Neither shows a two-leader narrow V at 40-45% of the height.
The visible pale limbs in the renders stay steeply ascending all the way to the crown edge, with no outward arching or droop. The reference's dark limbs fan out and droop near the edge.
The render crown edge is fine-grained but upright and uniform. It does not show the reference's layered, drooping sprays.
The render crowns are dense and mostly opaque. The reference crown is open, with sky and branches visible throughout.
Both render trunks are pale silvery grey and even-toned, with only faint horizontal marks and no furrows. This is consistent with the reference trunk.
Both render trunks visibly flare at the base. The darker base seen in the reference is absent, but its cause is undetermined, so this counts as acceptable variation.
Leaf shape cannot be resolved in the reference or at the renders' viewing distance, so there is no basis for comparison.
The render foliage is mid-to-bright green rather than the reference's pale yellow-green. The inventory classes leaf colour as seasonal variation.
The render crowns are nearly symmetric, while the reference is right-heavy. The inventory classes this asymmetry as variation.

render-0 (seed 1) and render-1 (seed 42) both show one tree with a narrow, spindle-shaped columnar crown and a pointed apex. The reference-0 tree has a broad, flat-domed, mushroom-like crown on a tall clear bole.
Render finish (bark shading, leaf density, lighting) meets or exceeds anchor-0's stylistic floor, so finish quality is not the limiting factor. The failures are in species morphology.
The pale grey, smooth-looking trunk with a flared base is the only strong beech cue the renders reproduce.
Neither seed would be read as an open-grown European beech. Their silhouette suggests a fastigiate poplar or hornbeam cultivar instead.

targeted.improved: Across the set, the renders with pale grey bark gained a believable pale grey trunk, and one of them gained a rounded crown with a V fork near the top of the bole, which gets closer to the reference's overall structure.
looks_wrong: Crown is a narrow upright ovoid, not a broad dome
Clear bole is short and the foliage is too dense, so almost no sky or limb structure shows through
targeted.missing: No render has the broad, flat-topped dome that is wider than it is tall, or the open, airy crown with dark limbs that rise and then arch out to near-horizontal, drooping at the edges. All of the crowns are too dense or too stiff.
